reasoning_summary: Counterexample-first pass over the riskiest concrete claims found nothing refutable. (a) Line 0002 (n*1_D > 0_D for all n in Z_{>0}) is the standard consequence of 1_D > 0_D in an ordered integral domain plus closure of the positive cone under addition; I could not build an ordered integral domain where some positive multiple of 1_D is <= 0_D, since the positive elements are closed under + and 1_D is positive (1_D = 1_D^2 is a nonzero square). (b) Lines 0005/0008: if Char D = p > 0 then p*1_D = 0_D, contradicting 0002, so the only remaining value is 0; this is exactly the definition of characteristic (least positive n with n*1_D = 0_D, else 0). (c) Line 0010: Char D = 0 makes n -> n*1_D injective (g(m)=g(p) implies (p-m)*1_D = 0_D implies p=m), and it is a unital ring homomorphism, so it is a monomorphism into D. (d) Lines 0012-0016: for m < p, p - m is a positive integer, so (p-m)*1_D > 0_D; distributivity of the integer-multiple map gives p*1_D - m*1_D = (p-m)*1_D > 0_D, hence g(m) < g(p) -- the inequality direction is right, and I could find no m, p making it fail. Remaining weaknesses are gaps rather than false statements: the proof never argues uniqueness ('the only monomorphism'), although uniqueness does hold because any unital ring homomorphism Z -> D must send n to n*1_D; and the problem statement's word 'onto' is a mismatch with the proof's 'into' (no monomorphism from Z is onto, e.g. D = R with g(n) = n). Since the proof's own asserted steps are all true and the intended theorem (Char D = 0, g an ordered-ring monomorphism into D) is correctly established, no counterexample exists to a claim the proof relies on.
